message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to delete my stepbrother's profile on my Nintendo Switch. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom were away. I brought my Switch with me because my school is more than an hour away, and I wanted something to do during the train commute every day. My stepbrother wanted to play on it, and since he was really into it, it actually helped distract him while I studied. So, I created a new profile for him on my Switch so he wouldn't mess up my saves. That seemed like a good idea at the time because it kept things organized and prevented any accidental deletions or changes to my games. When I got back to school, I started getting annoyed every time I had to click on my profile each time I started a game or went to the eShop. It was a minor inconvenience, but it annoyed me enough that I decided to delete his profile. I didn't think much about it at the time because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit, so I figured it wasn't a big deal. But then, during Thanksgiving, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. My stepbrother picked it up to play, and when he realized his Zelda save was gone, he started freaking out and even got a bit emotional. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because he knew my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. Now, I'm feeling a bit guilty because I didn't consider how much it might mean to him. So, is it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? Let's break it down. On one hand, the Switch is my property, and I have the right to manage who has access to it and under what conditions. Creating a separate profile was a responsible way to allow him to play without affecting my saves. However, deleting his profile without discussing it with him or giving him a chance to save his progress was probably not the best approach. I should have considered how important his gaming experience was to him. Even though it was a minor inconvenience for me to switch profiles, it was a significant emotional experience for him to lose his progress. My dad's reaction also indicates that he felt it was mean, which adds to the weight of the situation. Maybe I should have communicated with my stepbrother before deleting his profile. I could have explained that I wanted to keep things organized and offered to help him transfer his saves or find another way to manage the profiles. That way, I would have respected his interests and maintained a better relationship with him. In the future, it's important to think about how my actions might affect others, especially family members. Even if something seems like a small inconvenience for me, it could have a bigger impact on someone else. Communication and empathy are key in situations like this. So, in conclusion, while I had the right to manage my Switch, the way I handled it by deleting his profile without discussion was not considerate of his feelings and interests. It would have been better to find a solution that accommodated both of our needs.
